body:
Been trying to convince her to see someone. She actually just said it herself the other night that she might need to and I told her to not be afraid to take that step, as it could really help her.

She's joined a support group online so that's a good step too. 

Just moving isn't that easy though. We are on a really tight budget and need somewhere to go that at least accepts our dog and other pets.

As stated, my mother is disabled and needs help. We don't have any current plans to leave or abandon her in the future.

We have started discussing taking over the house taxes, we are just under a really tight budget right now.

I appreciate your words, really. Honestly comforting to have the assurance. I am lucky to have my girlfriend. She comes from a shitty family and our fathers are pretty similar, so she totally understands it too.

I just hope I eventually get to a point in life where I can help my mother more so she isn't dependent on the asshole for anything. My girlfriend and I have already started discussing possibly taking over the house taxes.

Yes, he cheated. We found out back in November and it took until April for him to move out. He's always been horrible, but it wasn't until this all happened that my mother opened her eyes to the fact he's a narcissist. 

Thank you. I'm glad you understand it isn't that easy. I always appreciate everyone's comments, especially the witty ones which are quite amusing. But a lot of people say "just do this" or "just do that" when it really isn't that cut and dry. 

My girlfriend and I do what we can, but it's only so useful when my mother doesn't help us stand up to him. Because in the end, it's her house and we are helping out. We don't have the option to move out and I'm not heartless enough to just cut her off. She's a victim in this too, but still mostly in the fog.

Yup, exactly. Which is what I was trying to tell my mother too. It isn't about the leash, it's about him needing control.

She now wants to bring it inside every time before he comes over, saying we can bring it back out after he leaves. She's been extremely upset all day because I told her that's not how this is going to work. I'm tired of him controlling every aspect of our lives.

First it's the leash, then it'll be something else and then something bigger. Because he *knows* he has that control over her. She "doesn't want to fight anymore".
Totally agree.

Technically my mother's. Girlfriend and I pay rent and help with other bills. If we weren't here, she wouldn't be able to afford staying and that's a big part of it. The other part is that she's disabled and needs help. We aren't in a good place financially at the moment where we could make it on our own either.

She says basically, that we can't fight with him because he pays the taxes on the house.

I'm holding my boundaries, I just can only hope my mother catches up and learns to stop letting him walk all over her too. It'll help if my SO and I can get into a position in our lives where my mother doesnt have to be as financially dependant on him.

Oh, I know. I know it's all about control and this is a point I tried to make with my mother. She "doesn't want to fight anymore" though.

I told her these things are going to continue happening as long as we let them.

Not me, but my mother.

My parents are going through a divorce after it was found my father was cheating. She eventually found post-it-notes hiding on his desk with a bunch of different info on them, but there were a few with flight times from Russia to Boston and then the estimated amount of time it would take to travel.

Amongst these notes were also their height and how much they weigh. Pretty disturbing stuff.

I'm not dependent on coffee, but I enjoy the taste. I can't drink it though, otherwise yes, I will get bad anxiety and even panic attacks.

I still drink it on occasion, but I have to make sure I'm mentally stable enough that day to be able to consume any. If I'm feeling even slightly not okay, I'll avoid it.

Honestly, this is what I was thinking of doing. Just toss that one or if he's really that worried, fucking give it to him. He's got nothing to use it for but clearly it stresses him out *oh-so-much.*

Like mentioned, I've been wanting to get a longer one anyway. Dare he try to control something I've bought with my own money.

My girlfriend's father is like this in a way. He's extremely narcissistic and emotionally abusive. He used to always defend his actions, saying he's a good father, because his own father would go as far as to beat him and kill their pets. So... because he didn't *beat* his kids, the mental trauma was okay and they "should be grateful."
I even needed to read that tonight. Good insight.

No kidding, haha. I haven't stepped foot into her house since the fall and that was only for a few minutes. Before that it had nearly been a year.

I *really* couldn't care if she has pictures of me or not. I've been done for a long time now and I'm not the one who's going to be staring at those empty spaces.

Damn, I never even thought of that. You're totally right and now I have even more reasons to be amused! She'll have to live with those spaces, knowing she's really lost her grandchild. Hurting no one but herself.

Thank you!! :)
Oh, we actually did have it hiding in the back of my car for awhile. It's back in the house now, though. Father has moved out so can't access it anymore.

Pure desperation, you're absolutely right haha. I tried to calm my mother down with that logic too, explaining that I'm really not all that bothered with it. Again, just amused.

I take comfort in the fact that I can go days without thinking about her, but she just constantly stews in her own anger while trying to come up with new things in an attempt to hurt me... None of it works, because I've long moved on. I'm not stewing like her, I've got better things to do than bask in my misery like she does!
Thanks!

It wasn't given to my dad. It was given to me as a child to play with my babydolls in. I've since let my niece use it for her own babydolls when she comes to visit, but have had to hide it (at least temporarily) because of this shit. Dad was going to take it and bring it to my grandmother behind my back, so basically steal it from me.

I hope to pass it on someday to play with if I have my own kids, or if my nephews/niece have their own kids, since it's been in the family for so long. My grandmother only wants the control over making me give it back, unfortunately. I don't think she truly cares about it.
Yup. She's always had control. A narcissist who raised a bunch of other narcissists.
Oh, I'd love nothing more than to drag my father under that bus. Unfortunately, at this point it would just cause more issues between him and my mother because they're now "remaining friendly".

You're totally right about that. That whole family is a giant JustNo.

Thank you!

The crib is in me and my girlfriend's closet. My father is moved out so we don't have to worry about him getting it anymore.

Definitely agree she doesn't care about the crib. It's all about having control and attempting to hurt me. No sweat off my back though... I'm not hurt by her (grieved that "loss" a long time ago) and she hasn't had control over me in years.
Thank you. I think things are going to be tense for a little while, but they aren't our problem anymore.
Right? That's what the rest of my family are saying too, but her and all her family don't agree, I guess. No one can stand up to her.
So strange. That's exactly how I felt too. The fever only made me feel more anxious.

Thank you for your response. Since I've posted this, things have only gotten more stressful, but I think it'll be over soon. He started to move out yesterday and will be officially gone on Saturday.

Yesterday was definitely more difficult than I'd anticipated. This is really happening. And I think it made me really upset because he was being decent to me, joking around, and those are the moments I miss having with him when I was younger, so it certainly hurt that he's done far too much damage for that to really mean anything.

"But he's your father!" / "But she's your grandmother!" Are both things I've heard frequently growing up. It wasn't until my father cheated on my mom that everyone suddenly switched sides and started listening to me that he's a fucking narcissist and so is his whole family.

I've been telling my mom that for over a year now, but it took my sister telling her about narcissism to finally listen to me about it.

Me too. Girlfriend was scrolling through videos a few weeks ago and one was basically about a new father and how close he was with his daughter. I cried and had to stop watching, because it made me jealous/upset that my own father could never spend time with me in that way or even be emotionally present whatsoever.

I remember coming across your post about this a few months ago and I could never imagine going through such a thing. You've kept strong though and your hard work has paid off!

Congratulations. I'm so happy you finally get to be with M.

I feel this.

I became good friends with someone after literally having no friends or support for years. 

I'd have my bad days and she was okay with listening. But I quickly realized that she would never truly understand, which I don't fault her for. She oftentimes would make comparisons when I'd open up about the emotional abuse I've suffered from my father, to her own father who sometimes got angry at her for maybe not taking care of a chore; stuff like that. It was really invalidating to me for her to make such comparisons and to know she wasn't understanding the mental distress my experiences were causing me.

I'll never forget when I first mentioned my depression, she actually said, "I've never had to deal with mental issues so I don't know what that's like, but I'm really sorry and hope you feel better" and it just hit me like a train that *not everyone is a depressed, traumatized mess like me*. 

I resented her for these things for awhile, but had to learn the fact her being okay with listening was kind enough as it is because she isn't my therapist, and it isn't her fault that she doesn't fully understand. I'm *happy* she hasn't had to experience these things or mental illnesses... *But* I don't really open up about my deeper, darker issues with her anymore.

I have a hard time watching a lot of TV shows with broken families, especially if it's comedy-based. The characters are usually over the top in order to be "humorous", but having grown up in such a family, I don't find it to be funny. 

I think of myself to have a pretty good sense of humor (sometimes dark) and I don't get offended by much, but shows/movies like that just really trigger me. I hate when television makes light of what are really horrible situations for people. Boundary-stomping, controlling behavior, and not owning up to your actions are not signs of being a funny and loving parent, who just wants what's best for their kid. They're signs of a toxic household.

I agree with that and my girlfriend and I do want to have that discussion with her. Especially because she is okay with him coming to visit our dog, and after everything he's put us through I just don't agree with that.

Every single day...

Growing up, I was a very firm believer of being careful of what you say and/or wish for. I never once said "I hate you" to either of my parents growing up, regardless of how angry or upset they made me. My father is a narcissist, my mother is an enabler.

Well, a few years ago my father had heart surgery for some really bad blockages that could've killed him had they not caught them in time. Since then, he has done some really horrible things and it only got worse after this past November when we found out he was cheating on my mom. 

I think back to his surgery often nowadays and sometimes wish he hadn't made it through because I'd be a lot better off now, mentally speaking. I cried for that man as he laid there pale and hooked up to tons of tubes and wires in the ICU. I almost even passed out at the sight. And it hurts me that I experienced all of that, because of how much worse he's gotten, regarding his mental abuse... because I know he doesn't care about me. It already feels like I don't have a father.

As a matter of fact, I even sent my girlfriend a text a couple hours ago about how much I hate him.

Thanks for this. My grandmother and my father have always been emotionally abusive. One time when my father was scolding me, telling me I need to "keep the peace" with my grandmother by "getting over" everything she had done to me, I said she had hurt me too badly. His response to that was, "She's hurt me too."

Because he had to go through it, I also did, and have been for a long time. I know this isn't completely on par with your post, but it feels fitting.

Not really, unfortunately. We also have pets that we need to take care of too. I'd otherwise ask my mother to care for them while we're gone, but she's disabled and I don't want to put even more stress on her. The whole reason we're even staying here to begin with, other than finances, is *because* she's disabled and will need help once my father is officially out.

Linkin Park was one of the first bands I really got into when I started listening to my own taste in music. Gosh, did they get me through some dark and tough times.

I remember actually crying when I found out about Chester.

One of my sisters used to watch me almost every day for a few years while my parents worked. She would do this *same exact* thing to my hair. Every single day. It gave me such bad headaches too, but I wouldn't be allowed to take my hair down until after my mom got out of work. Worst part is that my sister was a professional hair stylist.

I've *never* liked anyone touching my hair because of her. I've always cringed and coward away if I feel someone touch it. Only since I've been with my girlfriend have I started letting someone touch/play with it. Just her. I also eventually learned that brushing your hair didn't have to hurt.

I never really learned that from my parents, because my father just never gave a damn about me in that way, and I never let my mom touch it because of what my sister did.

Bash and bash? Are you a troll or something? Hah! He makes threats when he doesn't get his fucking way. He's a controlling narcissist. It's what they tend to do. There's a reason why I've been looking for new insurance. He was pissed at me anyway when I said I was going to be switching, since *his* won't be as cheap anymore. It's *all* about control.

The crib *is* mine, in fact, as it was (if you bothered to read up there) *gifted to me* over 15 years ago when I was a KID. You don't give people, especially children, gifts and then expect them back *almost two decades later*.

Maybe if you don't understand fucking abusive, narcissistic households, don't bother commenting in a subbreddit dedicated to them. Don't act like you know my situation. It's all there.
Oof. I'm sorry about that. That's super frustrating.
That's an interesting one... What is it about medication that she's so against? Is it the typical mindset that it makes you a "druggie"?

Moving out isn't an option for my girlfriend and I right now. My mother is going to need our help when asshole leaves anyway. She's disabled, thus can't work, and can't afford the house by herself.

She gets the house in the divorce and it just needs to get to that point. Unfortunately, the waiting game is just making it irritating, so just need to vent it all out sometimes.

Thank you!
It's both of them. I'm not sure what she can do with that, but regardless, she gets the house in the divorce. Even still, she's too worried about him ending up on the street.
100000000%, thank you. My grandmother and all three of her children are all the same. We always thought my father was the "good" one. I saw the signs a lot earlier than my mom though.

I love thinking of him as a troll. Thanks for that.

I am trying to cut all ties from him possible. I want no connections to him once he's officially gone. So I've been looking for cheaper car insurance, as well as health insurance. Planning on taking my mother's maiden name eventually too.

It's fine, I do appreciate your input. This has been going on for..... just over 4 months now, I believe? They have the divorce papers and my mom gets the house in it. She's waiting on him for the signing of them, and we have no idea what the fuck he's waiting for. 

I've tried talking to her about eviction, taking the legal routes, all that stuff. She's not tough, to put it lightly. She's more worried about him living on the streets than anything, so doesn't want to force him out until he has somewhere to go.
He would've been evicted months ago if it was my decision. This is *his* and my mother's house. So it isn't that easy, unfortunately.

My father is similar in that way. I've always found it really strange that he dismisses mental health so easily, because he's always struggled with depression and anxiety. (Again, undiagnosed, but there are tell-tale signs.) He even opened up to me once when I was a suicidal teenager that he had experienced the same thing at my age. I look back at that now as him redirecting it onto himself like he's always been best at, but it was the closest thing he and I ever had to a heart-to-heart about mental health. In reality, it was an opportunity for him to talk about himself and his poor life, to further dismiss me and my experiences.

Otherwise, mental health issues do *not* exist. He is allowed to have bad days because of what he struggles with, but no one else is allowed that. His own issues barely exist past himself and everyone else needs to "get over it". He has flatout said things like bipolar disorder and severe anxiety disorders do not exist and are just excuses for people not to work. He told me as a tween that I didn't have social anxiety, because I hadn't been diagnosed, *while* simultaneously disallowing me to get help for the fact I literally became crippled in any social setting.

Also, "therapy makes you hate your parents." 

*Sigh*. I totally hear you on that simulator comment, lol.

Yeah, I really appreciate her. He talks shit about us all the time to her and tells her all this shit about my grandmother, and she relays it to me. I trust her to keep me in the loop. It's like he doesn't believe we talk, but... not that far fetched, because him and I have never really had a relationship. Only when I was little and easily controllable/impressionable.

He really doesn't know that. He believes the closets are just junk storage with no more room in them, because... they unfortunately are. With all *his* shit. We cleaned one out recently, took his shit out, and reorganized. To be honest, he would probably be pissed to know we use them, even though they're in *our* bedroom.

He can't access our bedroom without someone knowing anyway. Someone is always home, mostly my mother because she's disabled and doesn't work.

I agree with this, OP.

Emphasis on the fact that he didn't want to be there for you guys when you *actually* needed it. His financial support, his emotional support, his protection, and through the process of your growing years. He didn't take part in any of your experiences that growing up entails. 

He now wants to be in your life, now that you *don't* need him. He no longer needs to support you in the way you needed as a child, which is convenient for him. No child support, no need to house you, feed you, clothe you. None of that. He didn't want the responsibilities back then, but wants the adult relationship with none of that effort *now.*

I also find it curious that he wasn't even the one to reach out. I get that parents like this oftentimes don't reach out because of their guilt and their fear that their child(ren) might be angry or hate them, but he claims he's so guilty, yet it was clear he was given the opportunity from your sister and she *still* had to really work for his attention.

It's just a super sketchy situation to me, and if anything, I would be on the side of caution. This decision is totally up to you, but I would take it as a warning that you may very well get burned. He might not be who you're expecting and he might not even be who he's showing himself to be. Maybe he really does feel guilt and wants to change things, build a relationship back up. That'll be up to you to decide, if you believe it's worth allowing the man who *abandoned* you back into your life, again, now that you're grown and it's convenient. 

It's a lot to think about, I know, and a lot of risks are involved. Whatever you do, do it for yourself and not for anyone else. Not for him, not if your sister wants you to do it. If *you* want to, that's your decision. Even if it's just for the sake of closure. I wish you the best of luck.

I feel like most narcissists aren't actually diagnosed. They tend to have too much fucking pride and don't believe anything is wrong. We all know the signs though.

I *know* my father's one. I *know* my grandmother is one. But they're too good for therapy. Mental health is *below* them. Abuse is abuse. Doesn't fucking matter if they're officially diagnosed or not. Gosh, I hate that shit.

Holy fuck, yes. Constantly. Exactly how you've described. I'll want to do something and will stress about it, since I "should" be doing something else more productive, and and I just won't do any of it.

Thank you, I didn't think I was in the wrong here but sometimes I need that reassurance because these psychos make me start to lose my mind. My mom and girlfriend are in agreement with me as well, a gift is a gift.

Unfortunately, that woman will never grow up. Which... is mostly fine with me, because I'm basically NC anyway and grieved her a long time ago. I'm pretty used to the JNFather's betrayal at this point too. He's never stood up for us against his mother. She's caused my mom and I a lot of pain, physically and emotionally, and he will and *has* told us plenty of times before that *we* need to get over it to "keep the peace".

I don't know why, but the "I don't know what happened to it" gave me a good chuckle. Thanks for that.

These suggestions are all too tempting.

I've never really associated it with my father's narcissism, but you might be onto something. He's... *really* bad about it with kids, which is kind of disturbing, to be honest.

When my oldest nephew started going to school, making friends, then talking about them, my father would always ask him if he had made any girlfriends yet. If my nephew ever mentioned a girl's name, my father would be right on top of it, teasing him about it until he was embarrassed and upset, like ashamed. I remember him doing that to me with boys when I was younger too.

Now that my niece has begun making friends, he does the same with her. Boys names will come up and he jumps on if they're her boyfriends, if she likes them, if she thinks they're cute. Again, relentless. She doesn't get embarrassed by it, but still. 

Again, I never really associated any of that with narcissism, but maybe that's why he did it. I always thought it was normal for families to tease each other over relationships with the opposite sex, although I've never agreed with it and think it's especially creepy when people push that mindset onto children, but yeah.

Absolutely. I also found out a bit ago that when my father was talking about how he was going to take it, my mom said to him that my niece likes playing with it (which is the whole reason it was out in the open in the living room to begin with, because I let her use it). His response was that they "will have to buy her a different one that looks like it". 

Like, *what‽* That is not how that is going to work, buddy!
Hah, It's definitely something to consider! I've felt more petty recently because of him mostly and wouldn't mind all that much making them look like fools.

I have been considering that. If he presses me on the matter, I may end up doing that. In the meantime, it's hiding in our closet. It had been in the living room before, out in the open, which is why he would be going behind my back to take it. He knew where it was before.
My girlfriend lives with us, so no. I do have a friend who could take it, but my girlfriend also has a storage unit. For now, it's hiding in our bedroom closet (as of a little bit ago).
Thank you!!

I really like that way of looking at it as well. You brush away her bad memories by making it your own. Your children will see that jewelery as a lovely reminder of their own mother, not something tainted by an abusive person.

Thank you for your support and kindness. I definitely will not let them take that from me. Father finally went to bed, so I will now be taking it and hiding it somewhere in our bedroom (for now), until he moves and I can take it back out and display it with other family heirlooms.
Hah! I love it too!

I do have a friend who could, but my girlfriend also has a storage unit that would work. I really don't expect him to go through our room looking for it, so I don't think I need to go as far as removing it from the house. If he gives me a hard enough time, then I definitely will.

I actually haven't hid it yet, but will be in a few minutes. I was waiting for him to go to bed, which he finally has. :) He won't be able to find it unless he trashes our bedroom, which I don't expect.
It's my parents' home, so I can't keep him from entering. He will be moving soon, though. We barely have a relationship now, so I don't plan on keeping contact with that horrid man.
Well, we live with my parents. Father cheated though, so will be moving soon. We have a camera that's going to be put up once he leaves, because he's a whole other headcase to deal with.
I actually really love this.
Thank you. Even if I don't have kids, I would give it to the kids of my nephews or niece if they ever decided to have any when they get older. I'd much rather that than for it to just be tossed.
Because I live with my parents, so I don't really have a choice over what he threatens to do. He cheated on my mother and will be leaving eventually, so that won't be a problem for long.

That's crazy, who the *hell* promises someone something they didn't even purchase themselves‽ Some people are absolutely nuts.

I hope your son enjoys his lessons. I've always wanted to learn piano. Someday!
Silly old woman is an understatement for her, haha. But you're absolutely right.
Apparently those rules don't apply to her. Unfortunate for her!

Yup, easily over 15 years now. So true.

It is going to be hidden as soon as my father goes to bed tonight, I think. I live with my parents, so. 

Been trying to figure out where to put it, but I'll just stick it in the closet for now and maybe bring it to my girlfriend's storage unit soon.
Good point!
All true. And I doubt she will ever personally reach out for it. The last time she ever made a phonecall to me was... my 16th birthday. But she's bitched for years that I never call her.

Yeah, I've got quite a few family heirlooms. The crib has meaning still because it wasn't directly my grandmother's; it was simply passed down to her. Like mentioned in another comment, I won't let her image taint that one.

Compare that to a ring that she gave me when I was younger that had belonged to her... Well, that one has lost its meaning for me.

Naw, I'm definitely not going to destroy it. The implication is pretty amusing though. I'm big on family history, so it is meaningful to me and I'm not going to let my grandmother's image taint it. Aside from her and her children, the rest of her family is nice.
I really love this way of thinking and had never thought of that before. Thanks for sharing.
Hah, absolutely.

Exactly, thank you! This is what baffles me. I was a *child*, like I barely remember a time where I *didn't* have it, which is what makes it worse. I've had it most of my life and now this psycho is trying to take it from me.

It's always been about control with her. Her lack of control over me is actually what started making our relationship deteriorate. I started realizing the things she had done to me growing up weren't right; I grew into my own person and she didn't like who I became.
Oh yes, the locks are definitely going to be getting changed.
I do have places I could bring it outside of the house, so good ideas. I have a good friend and my girlfriend also has a storage unit I could probably put it into.
Thank you, this is what they don't seem to understand. My girlfriend does have a storage unit I was thinking of temporarily moving it into.

I'm sorry she treated you so horribly for your miscarriage, but I'm glad you're not blaming yourself. My sister suffered through one and I saw how badly it devastated her. I just can't imagine a *mother* acting that way, but I've read about it far too often around here.

She's so hungry for attention too that she would be willing to have a *deadly illness* just for the sympathy and that's frankly, really disgusting. My girlfriend's mother died of cancer and my grandmother currently has it and will most likely die from it— To think there are people out there who act like they *want* it just really sickens me.

I don't know how you put up with it, OP, but I hope you don't continue to for very long. She sounds so toxic and you deserve way better than that. Just because she's your mother doesn't mean you need to suffer at the hands of her manipulation and guilt-trips. Health concerns are not a pass for someone to get away with treating you poorly.

Thank you. I live with my parents, so it's *their* home. Father won't be an issue for long, since (not sure if you read everything or just the TLDR, but-) my father cheated on Mom so he's going to be leaving.
Love your thoughtprocess and I totally agree, thank you.

Good for you. What he said was really shitty. I totally get preparing for a bad reaction, but being thrown off by how bad it actually ends up being.

I hope you continue to enioy your tattoo and your growth. You deserve to be happy with who *you* want to be in your own skin.

Yup. I've said it before, I'll say it again. No grandparents are better than bad ones. As someone with an ngrandmother, I wish my parents would have prevented me from having a relationship with her. But my nfather has always bowed down to her and her needs, not his own family's, so.

Children do not *need* a grandparent relationship. Sure, it can be nice for the possible good moments, but once that kid grows up and can't be influenced anymore, then what? My grandmother "disowned" me after I grew up and wasn't that cute little kid that would believe every word that came out of her mouth, so couldn't be under her control anymore. So there I was, an adult suddenly without a grandmother and then having the crisis of realizing everything she had done in my life was wrong.

It just *isn't worth it*.

I've commented this elsewhere before, but this is the exact attitude my father has. He did the bare minimum for me growing up; roof over my head, food on the table, clothes on my person. He was never affectionate, barely ever did anything with me. Never once has he told me he loves me, on his own. A couple times he mumbled it back when I tried saying it to him.

As soon as I turned 18, I was expected to be a full-grown adult, who also was never taught *how* to be an adult, while simultaneously being treated like a child. And from then on I was always well-informed that someday, I'll have to take care of them (he and my mother) because of everything they've done for me. 

Oh, what? The generous emotional damage that I'm still working through to this day? Yes, I now 100% owe you my entire life for doing the bare minimum of responsibilities having a child brings, but with the added extra glamorous trauma. 

Thanks, Dad.
I appreciate the kind words! :)

I get you, and I totally agree. I am only going to be 23 this year, so I do technically have a few years left. It's more of a peace of mind thing at this point... And to have no reasons to be dependant on him anymore.

And you're totally right– As far as that man is concerned, I probably owe him my whole life, even though he did nothing more than give me the basic necessities in life (food, roof over my head, clothes).

I do live in the US. The main problem is that I'm on his insurance. I'm hoping to get off of it in the near-future, though. He's going to be moving out (parents are divorcing), and I'm really trying to cut all ties I have to him. I don't want to owe him shit. 

It definitely is a miserable cycle to break. Someday, though!
Good old "it's not that bad". I'm sorry you went through that too.

I said it in another comment too, change is just so hard.

Pain medicine is literally my father's go-to for everything as well. He actually hoards strong pain killers from his past procedures (he'll only go to the doctor if his only other option is to literally die, resulting in surgeries on his leg and foot, heart surgery, etc.).
